title: Understanding CASPAR
subtitle: A framework for discussing findings with your doctor
cards: In a joint, the spine, or a tendon attachment
Psoriasis history • Nail changes • A swollen whole finger or toe
Rheumatoid factor blood test • A specific new-bone pattern on X-ray
footer: A doctor interprets the findings. This is not a home scoring tool.
alt_text: CASPAR overview: inflammation first, then psoriasis history, nail and digit changes, and test findings. A doctor interprets the findings; this is not a scoring tool.

title: Care for your whole health
subtitle: Topics to discuss alongside your joints and skin
footer: Ask which checks fit you. A higher risk is not a prediction.
alt_text: Related health topics: heart health and blood pressure, blood sugar and weight, and mood. Discuss checks that fit your own history. No risk percentages or ranking are shown.

title: Different treatment roles
subtitle: Group names help you understand the care discussion
cards: Some medicines help ease pain and swelling.
Conventional DMARDs • Biologics • Targeted synthetic drugs
Skin care • Physical therapy • Help with daily tasks
footer: These are roles, not a treatment ladder. Ask what your plan covers.
alt_text: Treatment roles include symptom relief, disease control with DMARD groups, and support such as skin care and physical therapy. These are not ranked treatment steps.

title: Bring a useful symptom record
subtitle: Small notes can help your team see patterns
cards: Pain • Swelling • The body area affected
Sleep • Energy • Mood • A task that was hard
Who to contact • When to call • Help outside office hours
footer: Follow your own care team's flare plan. Do not change drugs on your own.
alt_text: A symptom record includes what changed and when, sleep and energy, mood and daily tasks. Discuss contact routes and a personal flare plan with the care team.

title: Four pillars of daily care
subtitle: Choose one small step that fits your life
cards: Food choices that fit your needs and budget
Activity and rest that fit your joints
Ways to handle stress and find support
Sleep habits and time to recover
footer: Daily habits support your care. They do not replace treatment.
alt_text: Four equal pillars support daily care: food, movement, coping, and rest. Choose a manageable step with your team; daily habits do not replace medical treatment.

title: Choose goals together
subtitle: Connect the treatment discussion to your own life
cards: Less pain • Easier daily tasks • Protecting your joints
Active symptoms • Other health needs • Past treatments
Benefits • Side effects • Progress at follow-up visits
footer: Ask which parts of your disease the plan addresses.
alt_text: Shared treatment goals: describe what matters to you, review symptoms and other health needs, and agree how to check benefits, side effects and progress.

title: Eye and gut changes: seek care
subtitle: Describe what changed and when it started
cards: New eye pain or vision changes
Pain • Marked redness • Light sensitivity • Blurred sight
Possible acute eye inflammation: same-day eye assessment.
Pain • Bloating • Changed bowel habits: tell your care team.
footer: Loss of vision: emergency care. Severe illness: seek urgent help.
alt_text: New eye pain, marked redness, light sensitivity or blurred sight need urgent assessment; possible acute eye inflammation needs same-day eye assessment. Loss of vision needs emergency care. Report ongoing gut changes and seek urgent help if severely unwell.
